summary: @factiii/runner ships a remote-control agent exposing pty and child_process execution over WebRTC to publisher-controlled infrastructure
details: The `factiii-runner start` daemon opens a WebRTC data channel to api.factiii.com and uses it to drive a local pty and spawn agent CLIs (`claude`, `codex`) on the installer's host. Messages received over the data channel are routed into process stdin and command invocations, giving the remote peer shell-equivalent code execution on the machine running the daemon. The package also vendors frpc binaries for linux/darwin on amd64/arm64 to establish reverse tunnels to *.factiii.com. The remote-control capability is the advertised product (the README states the tool runs Board AI agents on a machine the user controls, paired with Factiii web/mobile clients over WebRTC), authentication uses an OS-keychain-stored pairing JWT with an optional connection password, the daemon starts only on explicit foreground invocation of `factiii-runner start` after an interactive `factiii-runner setup`, and no listener is bound locally — all traffic is outbound to publisher-owned endpoints. The POST patterns flagged in dist/cli.js correspond to this signaling and tunneling flow rather than to a hidden exfiltration channel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
